summary: @servicetitan/confirm preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: Version 41.3.3 of @servicetitan/confirm ships a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it via `execFileSync` to run a sibling file `math_init.js` at the tarball root. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript file (obfuscator.io-style shuffled string-array rotator `WV8StW`, hex-mangled identifiers, ~2000-entry constants table) whose behavior cannot be inspected statically. `package.json` declares `"files": ["dist", "src"]`, but `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are present at the tarball root outside that declared publish surface. A React confirm-dialog library has no functional need for an alternate language runtime or an opaque 727KB script; the pattern — downloading a second runtime at install time to execute an obfuscated bundled payload — is an alternate-runtime dropper that evades Node-based lifecycle scanners, and the tarball/manifest mismatch is consistent with a compromised publish rather than an intentional feature.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
